verdict.rationale: Feitian's own docs say the BioPass key matches fingerprints entirely on-device and that a lost key cannot be misused by anyone but the authorized user, which directly delivers the stolen-key protection. A FIDO PIN is also referenced, through PIN management in iePassManager. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of on-device verification, and detail on PIN enforcement across non-biometric models.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the key supports on-device user verification — a FIDO2 PIN or built-in biometric — so a stolen key alone cannot authenticate

citations.quote: The fingerprint is matched entirely on-device, so your biometric data never leaves the key — and losing the key poses no security risk.
The fingerprint module prevents any misuses of the token from people other than authorized user, and losing the key will cause no security risk at all.
